title: windlabel-box relative windings under frozen tests
subtitle: Step accuracy against the published hand windings; every rule and bar fixed before any box had a prediction
desc: Left: windlabel-box's split-chain step accuracy and its one-sided 95 % lower bound in six frozen tests on three scrolls, five passing the 0.92 lower-bound bar and one failing its 70 % keep floor. Right: on the 29 October boxes, windlabel-box against constraint-gauge's E1 on the same steps and against winding-phase at matched coverage; windlabel-box is ahead in every comparable pair, by 0.011 to 0.048.
alt: Two-panel chart. Left: six dots with downward whiskers for windlabel-box's step accuracy and lower bound in frozen tests from 24 to 29 October 2026 on PHerc0139, PHerc1667 and PHerc0172, all between 0.95 and 0.98, with lower bounds above a dashed 0.92 bar; the 24 October PHerc1667 split rule v1 test is drawn hollow and marked as failing its keep floor. Right: five paired dots, windlabel-box in blue against E1 in orange or winding-phase in green, each blue dot to the right of its partner; one row says E1 was not comparable.
caption: windlabel-box's step accuracy under frozen tests, and against two community winding tools on the same boxes (Model output against the published hand windings, 24 to 29 October 2026; numbers from docs/results.json windlabel_box_checks).
credit: Numbers from docs/results.json (windlabel_box_checks) and docs/tools/windlabel-box.md; hand windings and scans from the Vesuvius Challenge open data; E1 from pscamillo/constraint-gauge a72c423, winding-phase from millerandmuller/winding-phase 95583f3
foot: Whisker: one-sided 95 % block bootstrap lower bound. Axis starts at 0.88. Leads on the right are small; PHerc1667 is held out by position, not by scroll.
